items.stem: Which MySQL storage engine is required to enforce foreign key constraints and transactions?

options.rationale: Correct: InnoDB supports transactions and foreign keys; MyISAM does not.
MyISAM ignores foreign keys and has no transactions.
The MEMORY engine does not support foreign keys.
The CSV engine supports neither constraints nor transactions.

items.explanation: Correct: InnoDB supports transactions and foreign keys; MyISAM does not.

items.stem: Which TWO are guaranteed by wrapping statements in a committed transaction? (Select TWO)

options.text: Atomicity: all statements apply or none do
options.rationale: Correct: a transaction either commits fully or rolls back.

options.text: Durability: once committed, changes survive a crash
options.rationale: Correct: committed changes are persisted and survive restart.

options.text: The query runs faster than outside a transaction
options.rationale: Transactions are about correctness, not raw speed.

items.explanation: Correct: a transaction either commits fully or rolls back.

items.stem: Why is DECIMAL preferred over FLOAT for storing monetary amounts?

options.text: DECIMAL stores exact fixed-point values, avoiding binary rounding errors
options.rationale: Correct: DECIMAL is exact; FLOAT is approximate and can misrepresent money.
FLOAT handles large numbers; the issue is precision, not range.

options.text: DECIMAL uses less storage than FLOAT
options.rationale: Storage is not the reason; exactness is.

options.text: FLOAT is not supported in MySQL
options.rationale: FLOAT is supported but unsuitable for exact money.

items.explanation: Correct: DECIMAL is exact; FLOAT is approximate and can misrepresent money.
